title: Lemon Chiffon Cake
changes_from_base: Lemon juice replaces a third of the water and zest of 3 lemons goes into the batter; finished with a lemon glaze.
summary: This follows the classic chiffon method, with lemon juice replacing a third of the water and the zest of three lemons stirred into the batter, finished with a tangy lemon glaze instead of icing sugar.
equipment: 25 cm two-piece tube (angel food) tin, ungreased and unlined
stand mixer or electric hand whisk
wire rack or glass bottle for cooling upside down

ingredients.item: cake flour (or plain flour; see note)
ingredients.note: plain flour works with a slightly firmer crumb

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt, or table salt
large egg whites, at room temperature

steps.title: Heat the Oven
steps.text: Get the oven to 165°C (145°C fan) at least 20 minutes ahead of baking, setting a shelf in the lower third.

steps.title: Leave the Tin Ungreased
steps.text: Keep the tube tin completely bare - no grease, no lining. As the chiffon rises it needs to grip the sides of the tin, and that grip is what carries it to its full height.

steps.title: Make the Batter
steps.text: In a large bowl, combine the flour with 150g of the sugar, the baking powder and the salt. Form a well in the middle and tip in the egg yolks, oil, water, lemon juice, lemon zest and vanilla, whisking everything together until it turns smooth and glossy, about 1 minute.

steps.title: Whisk the Meringue
steps.text: Beat the egg whites with the cream of tartar on medium speed until foamy, then gradually add the 140g of sugar on medium-high speed, continuing until the meringue reaches stiff, glossy peaks that hold straight up. This cake relies on a well-built meringue to hold its height as it bakes.

steps.title: Fold Together
steps.text: Lighten the batter by whisking in a third of the meringue, then use a spatula to fold in the remainder across two additions, scraping down to the bottom of the bowl each time, until no streaks of white remain.

steps.title: Fill and Bake
steps.text: Transfer the batter to the tin, draw a skewer through it to pop any large air bubbles, and level the top. Give it 50-60 minutes in the oven: it is done when tall and deep golden, the top springs back when pressed, the cracks look dry rather than wet, and a skewer comes out clean.

steps.title: Cool Upside Down
steps.text: The moment it leaves the oven, flip the tin upside down onto its feet, or rest it over the neck of a bottle, and let it cool completely, about 2 hours. Turning it over like this keeps the soft, delicate crumb from sinking under its own weight while it's still hot.

steps.title: Unmould
steps.text: Slide a thin knife around the tin's sides and around the central tube, lift away the base, and ease the cake free from the bottom.

steps.title: Glaze the Cake
steps.text: Stir the icing sugar into the lemon juice until it forms a thick glaze that's still pourable, then spoon it over the top of the cake, letting it run down the sides. Leave it for 20 minutes to set before cutting into slices.

tips: Never grease the tin - a greased tin is the single biggest reason chiffon cakes slide back down as they cool.
Whisk the meringue to stiff, not soft, peaks; a soft meringue won't hold the cake's height.
Cool it upside down straight after baking, not once it's already started cooling the right way up.
Let the glaze set for the full 20 minutes so it stays on top instead of sliding straight off.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep covered at room temperature for up to 3 days, or in the fridge for up to 5 days. It freezes well unglazed, wrapped tightly, for up to 2 months; thaw at room temperature before glazing and serving.
